title: email-header-signature-cleanup-scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Working notes for cleaning and labeling inbound email corpora before using for conversational fine-tuning / retrieval. Focus: headers (From/To/CC), inline ‘On <date>’ forwarded blocks, multi-line signatures, legal disclaimers, and inconsistent line-wrapping produced by different mail clients.

Problem statement / why this matters:
- Models exposed to noisy headers and signature junk produce hallucinations when asked to summarize or extract actions.
- PII leakage (phone, emails, employee IDs) often resides in signature blocks; need consistent removal/labeling strategy.
- Line-wrapped quoted text often breaks sentence boundaries and confuses tokenizers — affects context windows and chunking.

Quick objectives (minimal, pragmatic):
1) Define deterministic rules to identify signature block boundaries for automated scrub + label sampling for manual review.
2) Define heuristics to collapse forwarded headers into a single standardized token (e.g., <FORWARDED_BLOCK>) while retaining minimal metadata (date/from).
3) Tag/remove PII in signatures & disclaimers but keep role/title/company lines for downstream intent parsing (if allowed by data policy).
4) Create a small hand-annotated seed (2k examples) to validate heuristics and tune regexes.

Notes / heuristics (first pass):
- Signature heuristics (priority order):
  * Detect common separators: lines that start with "-- ", "Thanks,", "Regards,", "Best," and variations. Consider language variants ("Merci,", "Saludos,").
  * If a paragraph at the end contains >=2 of: (phone number pattern) OR (email-like token) OR (company domain) OR (title keywords: "Director","Engineer","PM","Sr.") within 5 lines, mark as signature.
  * Single-line signatures (name + title) — still mark if followed by an email or tel pattern in next 1-2 lines.
  * If signature appears in middle of message (e.g., copied from forwarded content), then check for surrounding "On <date>" or lines starting with ">". If found, mark as forwarded-signature and handle differently.

- Forwarded / quoted blocks:
  * Normalize several common headers to a canonical token: patterns like "On <date>, <name> wrote:", "From:", "Sent:", "To:", "Subject:". Replace with single token sequence: <FWD_START date=YYYY-MM-DD from=domain.com?> ... <FWD_END>.
  * For privacy, strip full email addresses but keep domain and date when allowed. Example rule: replace "alice@example.com" -> "alice@<DOMAIN:example.com>" or simply "<EMAIL>" depending on policy.
  * For multi-level forwards (>>> chains), collapse up to 2 nested levels and insert "<NESTED_FORWARD_LEVEL=n>" metadata if needed for evals.

- Line wrapping and hyphenation:
  * Recombine lines that are broken mid-word by soft-wraps/hyphens. If a line ends with "-" and next line starts with lowercase, join without space.
  * If lines end with punctuation, preserve sentence break. If not, join with a single space.
  * Keep a small flag: "line_joined" to help downstream QA detect aggressive joins.

- PII tagging rules (signature-focused):
  * Phone numbers: standard E.164-ish patterns, also common local patterns. Replace with "<PHONE>".
  * Emails: replace with "<EMAIL>" unless policy allows domain-only retention.
  * Physical addresses: detect via numbers + street keywords -> "<ADDRESS>".
  * Employee IDs / internal tokens: pattern-based -> "<ID>".
  * Optional: keep job title + company string (e.g., "Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference") as text but tag as "title_company" for later filtering.

- Examples (annotator-friendly):
  1) Original:
     "Hi team,
      Let's ship this tomorrow.

      Thanks,
      Samira Khan
      Senior ML Engineer
      Redwood Inference
      +1 (415) 555-0123
      samira@redwood.ai
"
     Processed (policy: strip PII but keep title/company):
     "Hi team,
      Let's ship this tomorrow.

      <SIG_START>
      Samira Khan
      Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
      <PHONE>
      <EMAIL>
      <SIG_END>
"

  2) Forwarded chain: "On Tue, Aug 12, 2025 at 9:11 AM John Doe <john@acme.com> wrote:
      > FYI — the metrics look fine.
      > - John"
     Processed: "<FWD_START date=2025-08-12 from=acme.com>FYI — the metrics look fine. - John<FWD_END>"

Ambiguous / edge cases (notes to self):
- "Thanks — Sam" appearing mid-paragraph (e.g., in a quoted reply). Do not auto-trim unless signature-detection threshold met. Might need manual review sampling.
- Vanity sign-offs (emoji, ASCII art) — treat as signature if they occur at end; otherwise leave.
- Legal disclaimers that include long paragraphs (many lines). Some customers require disclaimers removed entirely; others want them preserved for compliance. Keep config toggle.
- Inline phone numbers in sentence: "call me at 5pm at (415) 555-1x23" — fuzzy matches. Keep robust regex + fallback to manual sample.

Annotation guidance for human labelers (seed creation):
- Label classes: [SIG_START,SIG_END], [FORWARD_BLOCK], [PII_PHONE], [PII_EMAIL], [ADDRESS], [TITLE_COMPANY].
- Provide examples in annotation UI: highlight exactly which lines count as signature. Prefer line-based labeling over token-level for efficiency.
- Unclear cases: mark with tag "uncertain" and a short reason. We'll sample all uncertain for adjudication.
- Time per doc target: 30–90s (aim 60s avg).

QA checks / metrics for heuristics:
- Precision / recall for signature detection on seed set. Target: precision >= 0.92, recall >= 0.85 (because false negatives are more harmful for privacy).
- PII redaction accuracy (phone/email): precision >= 0.98.
- Downstream metric: extractive QA F1 on summaries before vs after cleanup (should improve).

Sampling plan for seed annotations:
- 2k examples stratified by client domain (finance, healthcare, general).
- 30% forwarded chains, 50% single-author emails, 20% multi-author threads.
- Prioritize examples with non-US phone formats and non-English sign-offs in pilot.

Implementation notes / script ideas:
- Start with conservative regex + dictionary of sign-off tokens (en, es, fr).
- Run against 100k sample -> find top 500 uncertain by heuristic (low confidence) -> create adjudication batch.
- Maintain a small JSONL record for each processed message with fields: id, signature_lines_indices, piis_found, forwarding_detected, notes. (store separately; keep Drive doc small)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to handle signatures that include calendar links, booking URLs? Keep domain but redact query strings.
- Should titles like "Professor" be treated as PII if combined with name? (probably no, but note in policy)
- Confirm retention policy with Legal: can we keep company names + job titles? File action: ping legal in #legal-compliance.
- Add a periodic check to ensure regexes don't drift when new client domains appear.

Immediate next steps:
- Build initial pattern list and run on 10k sample (Marco).
- Create annotation UI template for line-based labeling (Elena).
- Draft short Confluence page summarizing the seed dataset and heuristics (Samira) -> link to CONFLUENCE-Email-Cleaning-Playbook.

Slack refs / quick links: #data-ingest, #labeling-ops, JIRA-4567 (email-cleanup).

Random scratch notes / heuristics snippets (for engineers):
- Regex phone: (\+?\d{1,3}[ -.]?)?(\(\d{2,4}\)|\d{2,4})[ -.]?\d{3,4}[ -.]?\d{3,4}
